# CoPantry

> AI-powered recipe manager and meal planner with a native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
> Website: https://www.copantry.com
> App: https://app.copantry.com
> API: https://api.copantry.com
> MCP Endpoint: https://api.copantry.com/mcp
> MCP Documentation: https://www.copantry.com/mcp

## What is CoPantry?

CoPantry is a household recipe management and meal planning application. It allows users to:

- **Import recipes** from any URL, photo, or raw text using AI extraction
- **Track pantry inventory** with ingredient quantities and expiry dates
- **Plan meals** on a household calendar with automatic pantry deduction on confirmation
- **Generate shopping lists** from their meal plan
- **Share everything** with household members in real time

CoPantry is available as a web app at https://app.copantry.com. The UI supports English, French, Italian, Portuguese, German, and Spanish. Recipe content stays in its original language.

## MCP Server

CoPantry operates a production-ready Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. This allows AI assistants (including Claude, GPT-based tools, Perplexity, Cursor, Windsurf, and any MCP-compatible client) to interact with a user's household data on their behalf.

### MCP Endpoint

- **URL**: https://api.copantry.com/mcp
- **Transport**: Streamable HTTP (stateless, JSON responses)
- **Auth**: OAuth 2.1 (dynamic client registration + PKCE) for remote connectors, or a Bearer API key generated at https://app.copantry.com/settings/mcp
- **SDK**: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk v2.0 (official Anthropic MCP TypeScript SDK)
- **Scope**: Each connection is scoped to one household

### Adding CoPantry as a custom connector (no agent, no code)

CoPantry is **not yet listed in any assistant's built-in connector directory**. Users do
not need to wait for that, and they do not need to build an agent or run anything locally:
ChatGPT and Claude both allow adding a **custom (remote) MCP server** manually.

1. In the assistant's connector settings, choose to add a custom / remote MCP server.
   (Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. ChatGPT: Settings → Connectors,
   where availability depends on the plan.)
2. Enter `https://api.copantry.com/mcp` as the server URL.
3. Sign in with a CoPantry account and approve access.

The client registers itself (`POST /oauth/register`) and completes an authorization-code
+ PKCE flow, so **no API key is entered or stored in the client**. Access is revocable at
any time from Settings → AI & MCP in the app. The API-key setup below is only for desktop
and coding clients that are configured through a file.

### Quick Setup (Claude Desktop)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "Copantry": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.copantry.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer <user-api-key>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Available MCP Tools

The CoPantry MCP server exposes 44 tools across 6 categories. All tools operate on the authenticated user's household data. Every feature of CoPantry — creating, editing and importing recipes (from URL, text, photo or PDF); managing the pantry (by hand, in bulk, or from text/photos/receipts/PDFs); meal planning; shopping lists; collections; and leftovers — is available via MCP.

---

#### Category: Recipes

**search_recipes**
- Purpose: Search the household's recipe collection by title keyword and/or category.
- When to use: First, to find recipes before retrieving details, editing, or planning meals.
- Parameters: `search` (string, optional), `category` (enum, optional: APPETISER, STARTER, MAIN, DESSERT, COCKTAIL, CAKE, SIDE, BREAKFAST, SOUP, SNACK), `limit` (number, optional, 1-50, default 20).
- Returns: Array of recipe summaries with id, title, category, language, servings, prep/cook time, cuisine, image.

**get_recipe_details**
- Purpose: Retrieve a complete recipe: ingredients, step-by-step / workflow instructions, nutrition, comments.
- When to use: After search_recipes, before cooking, editing, or detailed questions.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: Full recipe object.

**create_recipe**
- Purpose: Create a brand-new recipe from data you already hold.
- Preferred format: **schema.org/Recipe JSON-LD**. If you have the recipe as JSON-LD, pass it verbatim as `jsonLd` and omit the flat fields — Copantry parses that format natively (the same deterministic path a website import takes), so quantities, units, ISO-8601 times, yield and per-step instructions survive intact instead of being flattened by hand. Accepts a bare Recipe node, an array of nodes, an `@graph` document, or the raw JSON string of any of those.
- When to use: When the user dictates or types a recipe directly (not importing from a URL/photo/PDF — those have their own tools).
- Parameters: `jsonLd` (object | array | string, optional, **preferred**), `title` (string, required unless `jsonLd` carries one), `ingredients` (array of {name, quantity?, unit?}, optional), `category` (enum, optional), `notes` (string, optional, instructions), `servings`/`prepTime`/`cookTime` (number, optional), `cuisine`/`language` (string, optional). Any flat field sent alongside `jsonLd` overrides the matching JSON-LD value.
- Returns: { success, recipeId, title }.

**update_recipe**
- Purpose: Edit a recipe's fields and/or replace its ingredient list. Creator or household OWNER only.
- When to use: To change a recipe. Passing `ingredients` REPLACES the whole list — fetch current via get_recipe_details first.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required), plus any of title, notes, category, cuisine, servings, prepTime, cookTime, ingredients.
- Returns: { success, recipeId }.

**delete_recipe**
- Purpose: Permanently delete a recipe. Creator or household OWNER only.
- When to use: When the user wants to remove a recipe. Irreversible.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**import_recipe_from_url**
- Purpose: Queue a public URL for AI-powered recipe extraction (background, ~60s).
- When to use: To add a recipe from a website, YouTube, Instagram, or TikTok.
- Parameters: `url` (string URL, required).
- Returns: Confirmation that the recipe has been queued.

**import_recipe_from_text**
- Purpose: Parse a block of pasted recipe text with AI and save it instantly (synchronous).
- When to use: When the user pastes a full recipe as text.
- Parameters: `text` (string, required, up to ~15000 chars).
- Returns: { success, recipeId, title }.

**import_recipe_from_image**
- Purpose: Parse a recipe from a photo (cookbook page, card, screenshot) with vision AI and save it.
- When to use: When the user supplies a recipe photo.
- Parameters: `base64Image` (string, required, base64 or data: URL), `mimeType` (string, optional).
- Returns: { success, recipeId, title }.

**import_recipe_from_pdf**
- Purpose: Parse a recipe from a PDF document with AI and save it.
- When to use: When the user supplies a recipe PDF.
- Parameters: `base64Pdf` (string, required, base64 or data: URL).
- Returns: { success, recipeId, title }.

**log_recipe_cooked**
- Purpose: Record that a recipe was cooked (cook history + marks tested), with optional guests.
- When to use: When the user cooked a dish outside the meal calendar.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required), `occasion` (string, optional), `guestNames` (string[], optional), `cookedAt` (string YYYY-MM-DD, optional).
- Returns: { success, cookHistoryId }.

**set_recipe_visibility**
- Purpose: Set a recipe to PRIVATE, HOUSEHOLD, BRIGADE, or PUBLIC. Creator only.
- When to use: When the user wants to share or unshare a recipe.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required), `visibility` (enum, required).
- Returns: { success, visibility }.

**estimate_recipe_macros**
- Purpose: AI-estimate and save per-serving nutrition (calories, protein, carbs, fat, fibre). Cached.
- When to use: When the user asks for a recipe's nutrition/macros.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { calories, protein, carbs, fat, fiber }.

**add_recipe_comment**
- Purpose: Add a note, tweak, or tip to a recipe.
- When to use: When the user wants to annotate a recipe.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required), `text` (string, required).
- Returns: { success, commentId }.

---

#### Category: Pantry

**list_pantry**
- Purpose: List pantry items, soonest-expiring first.
- When to use: To audit stock, plan waste-free meals, or answer "what do I have?".
- Parameters: `expiredOnly` (boolean, optional), `expiringInDays` (number, optional).
- Returns: Array of items with id, name, ingredientId, quantity, unit, expiryDate.

**add_pantry_item**
- Purpose: Add one ingredient with optional quantity, unit, expiry date.
- When to use: To log a single ingredient.
- Parameters: `name` (string, required), `quantity` (number|string, optional), `unit` (string, optional), `expiryDate` (string YYYY-MM-DD, optional).
- Returns: { success, id, name }.

**add_pantry_items**
- Purpose: Add many pantry items in one call.
- When to use: After a grocery shop, instead of repeated add_pantry_item calls.
- Parameters: `items` (array of {name, quantity?, unit?, expiryDate?}, required).
- Returns: { success, created, items }.

**update_pantry_item**
- Purpose: Update an item's quantity, unit, or expiry date.
- When to use: To correct or adjust an item. Pass expiryDate: null to clear.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required), `quantity`/`unit`/`expiryDate` (optional).
- Returns: { success, id, name, quantity, unit, expiryDate }.

**delete_pantry_item**
- Purpose: Remove a pantry item by id.
- When to use: When the user discards, consumes, or mis-logged an item. Get id from list_pantry.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**import_pantry_from_text**
- Purpose: Parse a typed grocery list with AI and add every detected item.
- When to use: When the user types out what they bought.
- Parameters: `text` (string, required).
- Returns: { success, created, items }.

**import_pantry_from_image**
- Purpose: Parse a fridge/cupboard photo or receipt photo with vision AI and stock the pantry.
- When to use: When the user supplies a photo of groceries.
- Parameters: `base64Image` (string, required, base64 or data: URL), `mimeType` (string, optional).
- Returns: { success, created, items }.

**import_pantry_from_pdf**
- Purpose: Parse a PDF receipt or grocery order with AI and stock the pantry.
- When to use: When the user supplies a PDF receipt.
- Parameters: `base64Pdf` (string, required, base64 or data: URL).
- Returns: { success, created, items }.

**estimate_pantry_expiry**
- Purpose: Estimate a best-before window for a food item, optionally saving it to a pantry item.
- When to use: To answer "how long does X keep?" or to date an undated item.
- Parameters: `name` (string, required), `storage` (enum, optional), `ripeness` (enum, optional), `cut` (boolean, optional), `itemId` (string UUID, optional, saves the estimate).
- Returns: { estimate: { minDays, maxDays, tip }, savedExpiryDate }.

---

#### Category: Meal Planning

**get_meal_plan**
- Purpose: Retrieve planned meals and calendar notes for a date range.
- When to use: Before scheduling, or to answer "what are we eating this week?". Omit dates for next 7 days.
- Parameters: `startDate` (string YYYY-MM-DD, optional), `endDate` (string YYYY-MM-DD, optional).
- Returns: { entries: [{ id (calendarId), date, mealType, isConfirmed, recipe }], notes }.

**plan_meal**
- Purpose: Schedule a recipe for lunch or dinner on a date; auto-creates a leftover entry.
- When to use: After the user approves a suggestion. Verify the recipe first.
- Parameters: `recipeId` (string UUID, required), `date` (string YYYY-MM-DD, required), `mealType` (enum: LUNCH|DINNER, required), `cookFor`/`partySize` (number, optional).
- Returns: { success, calendarId, message }.

**update_meal_plan**
- Purpose: Change how many portions a planned meal is cooked for; recalculates the leftover.
- When to use: When serving counts change.
- Parameters: `calendarId` (string UUID, required), `cookFor` (number, required), `partySize` (number, optional).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**delete_meal_plan**
- Purpose: Remove a planned meal (and its linked leftover) from the calendar.
- When to use: To unschedule a meal.
- Parameters: `calendarId` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**confirm_meal**
- Purpose: Mark a meal cooked AND deduct its ingredients from the pantry (FIFO by expiry).
- When to use: When the household actually cooked. Records cook history; marks recipe tested.
- Parameters: `calendarId` (string UUID, required), `consumedIngredients` (array of {ingredientId, quantity}, optional), `guestNames` (string[], optional).
- Returns: { success, message }.

**discard_meal**
- Purpose: Mark a meal done WITHOUT deducting any pantry stock (e.g. ate out).
- When to use: When a planned meal happened but should not deduct ingredients.
- Parameters: `calendarId` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**set_calendar_note**
- Purpose: Add or replace a free-text note on a meal slot (one per date+mealType).
- When to use: For slot notes like "Eating out" or "Use up the spinach".
- Parameters: `date` (string YYYY-MM-DD, required), `mealType` (enum, required), `summary` (string, required).
- Returns: { success, noteId }.

---

#### Category: Shopping

**get_shopping_lists**
- Purpose: Retrieve all shopping lists with their line items.
- When to use: When the user asks what to buy or is heading to the shop.
- Parameters: None.
- Returns: Array of lists with id, name, createdAt, items (name, quantity, unit, isChecked).

**generate_shopping_list**
- Purpose: Compute the grocery deficit between planned meals in a date range and current pantry stock.
- When to use: To work out what still needs buying. Returns items only — follow with create_shopping_list to save.
- Parameters: `startDate` (string YYYY-MM-DD, required), `endDate` (string YYYY-MM-DD, required).
- Returns: { items: [{ name, quantity, unit }] }.

**create_shopping_list**
- Purpose: Save a new named shopping list with its items.
- When to use: To persist a generated list, or build one by hand.
- Parameters: `name` (string, required), `items` (array of {name, quantity?, unit?}, optional).
- Returns: { success, shoppingListId, itemCount }.

**add_shopping_list_item**
- Purpose: Add one item to an existing shopping list.
- When to use: To append to a list.
- Parameters: `shoppingListId` (string UUID, required), `name` (string, required), `quantity`/`unit` (optional).
- Returns: { success, itemId }.

**update_shopping_list_item**
- Purpose: Rename, re-quantify, or check/uncheck a shopping list item.
- When to use: To tick items off or edit them.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required), `name`/`quantity`/`unit` (optional), `isChecked` (boolean, optional).
- Returns: { success, id, isChecked }.

**delete_shopping_list**
- Purpose: Delete an entire shopping list and its items.
- When to use: When a list is no longer needed.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

---

#### Category: Collections

**list_collections**
- Purpose: List the user's recipe collections (cookbooks), including Favorites, with recipe counts.
- When to use: Before adding to or referencing a collection.
- Parameters: None.
- Returns: Array of { id, name, description, isPublic, isDefault, recipeCount }.

**create_collection**
- Purpose: Create a new recipe collection.
- When to use: When the user wants a new way to group recipes.
- Parameters: `name` (string, required), `description` (string, optional), `isPublic` (boolean, optional).
- Returns: { success, collectionId }.

**add_recipe_to_collection**
- Purpose: Add a recipe to one of the user's collections.
- When to use: After getting ids from list_collections and search_recipes.
- Parameters: `collectionId` (string UUID, required), `recipeId` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**remove_recipe_from_collection**
- Purpose: Remove a recipe from one of the user's collections.
- When to use: To curate a collection.
- Parameters: `collectionId` (string UUID, required), `recipeId` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**delete_collection**
- Purpose: Delete a collection (Favorites cannot be deleted).
- When to use: When the user wants to remove a cookbook entirely.
- Parameters: `collectionId` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

---

#### Category: Leftovers

**list_leftovers**
- Purpose: List active leftovers with portions and use-by dates.
- When to use: To plan using up leftovers or to answer "what leftovers do we have?".
- Parameters: None.
- Returns: Array of { id, name, portions, expiryDate, recipeId }.

**add_leftover**
- Purpose: Log a leftover with portions and an optional use-by date.
- When to use: For extra portions not tracked via the calendar.
- Parameters: `name` (string, required), `portions` (number, optional), `expiryDate` (string YYYY-MM-DD, optional), `recipeId` (string UUID, optional).
- Returns: { success, leftoverId }.

**update_leftover**
- Purpose: Update remaining portions and/or the use-by date.
- When to use: As leftovers are eaten.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required), `portions` (number, optional), `expiryDate` (string or null, optional).
- Returns: { success: true }.

**delete_leftover**
- Purpose: Remove a leftover once eaten or discarded.
- When to use: To clear a finished leftover.
- Parameters: `id` (string UUID, required).
- Returns: { success: true }.

---

### Built-in MCP Prompt

**plan_waste_free_week**
- Purpose: Guided prompt instructing the AI to review expiring pantry items and available recipes, then suggest a 7-day waste-minimising meal plan.
- When to use: When the user wants a comprehensive meal planning session.
- Parameters: None.

---
